title: The empty cut

data.source: The R4 rotor of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md with memory coupling, twelve occasions, integrated here at three step sizes and four window widths. Adapted from colloquy/lab/philosophical/cut_mereology.py.

phoenix_status: MATHEMATICS.md section VII, status ONTOLOGY: "the present is an empty boundary carrying conditions inherited from that history". NOT_DECIDABLE_REGISTER.md row ND-4 records as shared structure that "every instrument that locates the cut carries content (Ashes note 06)" and that the emptiness "has no measurement"; under breaking intervention it says "none for the ontology"; and it records that "the formal forms are decidable and have failed (MEAS2, CARD, H1CARD)".
prediction: Whatever sits inside the cut shrinks with the step, the event work at the cut does not, and a thick cut of width w gives the same record as the thin one once w is small; so R1 to R6 cannot tell an empty boundary from a short thick one.
baseline: An ordinary hybrid ODE with an instantaneous reset (where "the event has no duration" is a convention), and as a decoy the thick-cut rotor, which has something in the cut by design.
why: In the toy rotor nothing with size sits in the cut, yet a work term is booked there that does not shrink. A thick cut gives the same record as the thin one once it is narrower than the instrument. So nothing in R1 to R6 tells an empty boundary from a short thick one. Phoenix files this as ONTOLOGY and not decidable (ND-4).
variant: V-philosophical-2 (the thick cut): a museum experiment, not the owner's CRR
would_make_it_testable: An instrument finer than the window w, and a measure of the event work that does not depend on the model of the two neighbouring occasions.
